name: Enforcement trends

subjectOf.text: Almost 300 deferred prosecution agreements have been executed since 2003, whereas before 2003 they were rarely used.
subjectOf.abstract: Almost 300 DPAs have been executed since 2003. Before 2003, DPAs were rarely used.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857

subjectOf.text: The sharp proliferation of non and deferred prosecution agreements after 2002 is explained by a cluster of events: the collapse of Enron, the dismantling of Arthur Andersen, the creation of the Corporate Fraud Task Force, and the Thompson Memorandum.
subjectOf.abstract: The proliferation of N/DPAs after 2002 can be explained by a num- ber of factors, including the collapse of Enron, the dismantling of Arthur Ander- sen, the establishment of the Corporate Fraud Task Force, and the Thompson Memorandum.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy Lacine, The Effect of Deferred and Non-Prosecution Agreements on Corporate Governance Evidence from 1993-20 (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2486570

subjectOf.text: Corporate governance provisions in non and deferred prosecution agreements increased significantly over the decade to 2013, raising prosecutors' influence over corporate governance to unprecedented levels.
subjectOf.abstract: find that corporate governance provisions in N/DPAs significantly increased in the last decade, boosting prosecutors' influence over corporate governance to un- precedented levels.
